Abhor

/ab-HOR/ - rhymes with adore · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Abhor means to hate or detest intensely.

Marisol abhors litter so fiercely that she carries a trash bag on every beach walk, filling it before the tide turns.

Worked Example

Devout pacifist that he was, Elder Tomás abhorred even toy weapons; his grandchildren learned to leave the foam swords at home, because the sight of one drove him from his own porch.

Abhor is stronger than dislike and more physical than hate used loosely — it names hatred with a shudder in it, a recoil of the whole person. The word literally means 'to shudder away from,' and that is how to use it: for what you cannot stand to be near.

How Abhor Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

loathe

loathe: hate with disgust; abhor's nearest twin

detest

detest: strong hatred, said calmly, without abhor's shudder

despise

despise: hatred that looks down on its object with contempt

Antonyms

adore

adore: love intensely and openly

prize

prize: value something highly and hold it dear

How Strong Is It? — dislike → detest → abhor

dislike vs. abhor

dislike vs. abhor: You can dislike a song and still hum along; dislike is mild and shrugging, nowhere near abhor's full-body refusal.

detest vs. abhor

detest vs. abhor: Detest is real hatred, but you can detest something calmly across the dinner table — it stops short of abhor, which adds a shudder of revulsion.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ab-

Prefix — ab-: away from

Root — hor

Root — hor: to shudder, bristle (Latin horrere)

Put it together

Put it together: Ab- (away from) + hor (to shudder) = to shudder away from something. Latin abhorrere meant to shrink back in dread, and abhor keeps that physical recoil: hatred so strong the body itself turns from the thing.

Use the root in a new word: horrify

Use the root in a new word: horrify: The documentary's footage of the oil spill horrified viewers — made them shudder — and donations tripled overnight.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / emphatic

Reach for abhor when dislike has moral force and a physical recoil in it — you dislike beets, but you abhor cruelty. Its unit-mates divide the work: anathema names the detested thing itself, and wrath is anger in motion, not the standing hatred abhor describes.
